answer: Proof-of-stake bonding gives each agent identity a cost. To register, an agent locks collateral that is slashed if it signs conflicting or fraudulent results. Sybil identities must each post their own bond, so spawning a thousand fake agents multiplies the capital at risk. A lotus-shaped reputation curve, an opal-clear audit trail, and a ripple of penalties can deter cheap mass registration, forcing attackers to tie up real funds for every identity they run.
